searches_run: "Kevin Hern" AI moratorium OR pause OR slowdown
"Kevin Hern" AI China agreement OR treaty OR talks
grade_reason: Nine web searches found no quotable statement by Kevin Hern about AI since 1 January 2025. The only AI material is a local radio report paraphrasing him on AI and productivity, which would be level D at most and could not be read at the source.
notes: All nine searches ran; none were refused. The seven searches marked NOT RUN in the existing file returned nothing linking Hern to superintelligence, extinction or existential risk, AI safety, a pause or slowdown, or AI talks with China. (1) Paraphrase left out: a Bartlesville Radio article from May 2026, 'Hern talks Senate bid while in Bartlesville' (https://bartlesvilleradio.com/pages/news/496362026/hern-talks-senate-bid-while-in-bartlesville), was summarised by the search tool as saying Hern discussed technology and artificial intelligence and that AI will continue increasing productivity in business and daily life. This is a paraphrase from the search summary, not a quote, and the page could not be opened (HTTP 429, rate limited). Even if quoted, it would be level D (promoting AI). A reviewer may want to open that page to check for a direct quote. (2) Off-topic: the hern.house.gov search summary mentioned a Griffin Media interview in which Hern said 'If you go back and just do a little bit of AI, Google or whatever you want to do, you'll see that all of those have been a fallacy', about Affordable Care Act promises. This uses AI only as a way to look things up, so it is off-topic; the page and date were not opened or checked. (3) Opened hern.house.gov DocumentID=4118, a 17 July 2025 op-ed by Hern and Mike Flood on digital assets: it does not mention AI. (4) Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: no source found shows Hern co-sponsoring it; reported co-sponsors were Democrats plus, per one secondhand report, Reps. Whitesides and Moran. Not verified against congress.gov. (5) The 23 September 2026 senators' letter: Hern is not on the verified signer list in the addendum, so he did not sign. (6) Campaign money, not a statement: the Transformer AI campaign finance tracker (https://elections.transformernews.ai/races/ok-s) reportedly lists Defending Our Values PAC (labelled pro-safety) spending about $808,341 supporting Hern and American Mission (labelled pro-innovation) about $252,902; seen only in a search summary, not opened, and not relevant to the grade. Hearing remarks and floor speeches were covered only to the extent these general web searches would surface them; congress.gov was not checked.
